args.description: A board is a width×height rectangle of cells and holds exactly the game's mine_count mines once laid.

args.given_when_then: Given a Custom configuration with valid width W and height H When the mine count is between 10 and (W−1)×(H−1) inclusive Then it is accepted, and When it is below 10 or above (W−1)×(H−1) Then the configuration is refused

args.title: Invalid custom leaves current game unchanged
args.description: A refused Custom configuration shows a message and does not alter or abandon the current game.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in any status When the player submits a Custom configuration outside the limits Then a validation message is shown and the current game, its board, timer and counter remain unchanged

args.title: Mines laid on first open
args.description: No mines exist on the board until the first cell is opened.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Ready status with no mines laid When the player opens the first cell Then the mines are laid at that moment, and before that moment no cell holds a mine

args.title: First click is safe
args.description: The first opened cell never holds a mine.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Ready status When the player opens any cell as the first open Then that cell holds no mine and the game does not end in a loss

args.title: Ready to Playing transition
args.description: The first open moves the game from Ready to Playing.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Ready status When the player opens a hidden unflagged cell Then the game status becomes Playing

args.title: Open a hidden unflagged cell
args.description: Opening a Hidden cell sets its state to Opened.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Ready or Playing status and a cell in Hidden state When the player opens it Then the cell state becomes Opened (or Detonated if it holds a mine)

args.title: Neighbour mine count
args.description: An opened safe cell's number equals the count of mines among its up to 8 neighbours.
args.given_when_then: Given an interior safe cell with K mines among its 8 neighbours When it is opened Then its adjacent mine count is K (0 to 8)

args.title: Edge and corner neighbours
args.description: Edge cells have 5 neighbours and corner cells 3; only existing neighbours are counted.
args.given_when_then: Given a safe cell on an edge (5 neighbours) or a corner (3 neighbours) When its adjacent mine count is computed Then only the neighbours that exist within the grid are counted

args.title: Cascade on zero
args.description: Opening a zero cell automatically opens all its neighbours, repeating for further zeros.
args.given_when_then: Given a hidden safe cell with adjacent mine count 0 When it is opened Then all its hidden neighbours are opened, and any opened neighbour with count 0 opens its neighbours in turn

args.title: Cascade stops at numbered cells
args.description: Numbered cells are opened by a cascade but do not propagate it.
args.given_when_then: Given a cascade in progress When it opens a cell with adjacent mine count of 1 or more Then that cell is opened and its own neighbours are not opened by the cascade

args.title: Cascade skips flagged cells
args.description: A cascade never opens a flagged cell.
args.given_when_then: Given a cascade in progress and a neighbouring cell in Flagged state When the cascade reaches it Then the cell remains Flagged and is not opened

args.title: Toggle flag
args.description: Flagging toggles a hidden cell between Hidden and Flagged.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Ready or Playing status When the player flags a Hidden cell Then it becomes Flagged, and When the player flags a Flagged cell Then it becomes Hidden

args.title: Flagged cell cannot be opened
args.description: Opening a flagged cell is refused until it is unflagged.
args.given_when_then: Given a cell in Flagged state When the player tries to open it Then the cell stays Flagged and nothing is revealed, and When the player unflags it and opens it Then it is opened

args.title: Unlimited flags
args.description: The number of flags is not limited by the mine count.
args.given_when_then: Given a game whose flags placed already equals its mine count When the player flags another Hidden cell Then the flag is placed

args.title: Remaining mines counter
args.description: Remaining mines = total mines − flags placed, which may be negative.
args.given_when_then: Given a game with M mines and F flags placed When the counter is calculated Then it equals M − F, including negative values when F > M

args.title: Chord with matching flags
args.description: Chording an opened number whose adjacent flags equal its number opens all other hidden unflagged neighbours.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Playing status and an Opened cell with number N and exactly N flagged neighbours When the player chords it Then all its Hidden unflagged neighbours are opened (with cascades as applicable)

args.title: Chord with mismatched flags does nothing
args.description: If adjacent flags do not equal the number, chording has no effect.
args.given_when_then: Given an Opened cell with number N and a number of flagged neighbours different from N When the player chords it Then no cell changes state

args.title: Chord with wrong flag loses
args.description: If a misplaced flag makes a chord open a mine, the game is lost.
args.given_when_then: Given an Opened cell with number N and N flagged neighbours, one of which is not a mine When the player chords it Then the unflagged mine neighbour is opened, becomes Detonated and the game status becomes Lost

args.title: Timer starts at first open
args.description: The timer starts at the first open and counts whole seconds; it reads 0 before that.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Ready status with elapsed seconds 0 When the player opens the first cell Then the timer starts and elapsed seconds increases by 1 each second

args.title: Timer cap at 999
args.description: Elapsed seconds never exceeds 999.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Playing status with elapsed seconds 999 When further time passes Then elapsed seconds stays at 999

args.title: Timer freezes on end
args.description: The timer stops when the game is won or lost.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Playing status When the game becomes Won or Lost Then elapsed seconds is frozen at its current value

args.title: Opening a mine loses
args.description: Opening a mine ends the game in a loss and records the struck cell.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Playing status When the player opens a Hidden cell holding a mine Then the cell becomes Detonated, it is recorded as the struck cell and the game status becomes Lost

args.title: Win condition
args.description: The game is won when every non-mine cell is opened, regardless of flags.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Playing status When the last non-mine cell is opened Then the game status becomes Won whether or not the mines are flagged, and while any non-mine cell is unopened the game is not Won

args.title: Auto-flag on win
args.description: On a win all mines become flagged and the remaining-mines counter becomes 0.
args.given_when_then: Given a game that has just become Won When the win is recorded Then every mine cell is set to Flagged, flags placed equals the mine count and the remaining-mines counter is 0

args.title: New best time
args.description: A win on a standard difficulty faster than the stored best replaces it.
args.given_when_then: Given a stored best time of B seconds for a standard difficulty When the player wins a game of that difficulty in T seconds with T < B Then the best time becomes T for that difficulty on this device

args.title: First win sets best time
args.description: With no stored best, a standard win becomes the best time.
args.given_when_then: Given no best time stored for a standard difficulty When the player wins a game of that difficulty in T seconds Then a best time of T is recorded for that difficulty

args.title: Slower or equal win keeps best
args.description: A win not faster than the stored best does not change it.
args.given_when_then: Given a stored best time of B seconds for a standard difficulty When the player wins in T seconds with T >= B Then the best time remains B

args.title: Custom games record no best time
args.description: Wins on Custom difficulty never create or update a best time.
args.given_when_then: Given a game on Custom difficulty When the player wins it Then no best time is created or changed

args.title: Lost or abandoned games record no best time
args.description: Only wins can produce a best time.
args.given_when_then: Given a game that ends Lost or Abandoned When it ends Then no best time is created or changed

args.title: Board lock after end
args.description: After a win or loss only a new game is accepted.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Won or Lost status When the player opens, flags or chords any cell Then no cell, counter or timer changes, and When the player starts a new game Then it is accepted

args.title: Opening an opened cell is ignored
args.description: Opening an already opened cell changes nothing silently.
args.given_when_then: Given a cell in Opened state When the player opens it Then nothing changes and no message is shown

args.title: Flagging an opened cell is ignored
args.description: Flagging an opened cell changes nothing silently.
args.given_when_then: Given a cell in Opened state When the player toggles a flag on it Then the cell stays Opened, flags placed is unchanged and no message is shown

args.title: Chording a hidden cell is ignored
args.description: Chording a hidden cell changes nothing silently.
args.given_when_then: Given a cell in Hidden state When the player chords it Then no cell changes state and no message is shown

args.title: Restart via smiley
args.description: Pressing the smiley abandons the current game without score and deals a fresh board of the same difficulty.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Ready or Playing status When the player presses the smiley Then that game becomes Abandoned with no best time recorded and a new Ready game of the same difficulty with all cells Hidden, timer 0 and counter equal to its mine count is created

args.title: Smiley after end starts new game
args.description: Pressing the smiley on a Won or Lost game starts a fresh game without altering the finished one.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Won or Lost status When the player presses the smiley Then the finished game keeps its outcome and a new Ready game of the same difficulty is created

args.title: Changing difficulty
args.description: Choosing a difficulty abandons the current game and starts a new one with the chosen settings.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Ready or Playing status When the player chooses a valid difficulty Then the current game becomes Abandoned with no score and a new Ready game with the chosen width, height and mine count is created

args.title: Leaving abandons the game
args.description: Closing the game abandons any game in progress and records nothing.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Ready or Playing status When the player closes the game Then it becomes Abandoned and no best time is recorded

args.title: Abandon only from Ready or Playing
args.description: Only Ready or Playing games can become Abandoned; Won and Lost are final.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in Ready or Playing status When it is abandoned Then its status becomes Abandoned, and Given a game in Won or Lost status When an abandon is triggered Then its status remains Won or Lost

args.title: Game status transitions
args.description: Allowed transitions: Ready→Playing, Playing→Won, Playing→Lost, Ready/Playing→Abandoned; no others.
args.given_when_then: Given a game in any status When a transition is requested Then only Ready→Playing, Playing→Won, Playing→Lost and Ready or Playing→Abandoned are allowed and all other transitions are refused

args.title: Cell state transitions
args.description: Cell states: Hidden↔Flagged, Hidden→Opened, Hidden→Detonated; Opened and Detonated are final (except auto-flag on win).
args.given_when_then: Given a cell When its state changes Then only Hidden↔Flagged, Hidden→Opened (safe) and Hidden→Detonated (mine) are allowed, and an Opened or Detonated cell never returns to Hidden or Flagged

actions.name: open_cell
actions.description: Opens the cell at zero-based (row, column), and is allowed only while status is Ready or Playing. On the first open of a Ready game, mines_laid becomes True and exactly mine_count mines are placed at random on cells other than the opened one. Every cell's adjacent_mine_count is then set to its mines among the existing up-to-8 neighbours, status becomes Playing and started_at is set. A Hidden safe cell becomes Opened; if its count is 0 the cascade opens Hidden neighbours, repeating through zeros, stopping at numbered cells and skipping Flagged cells. If the cell holds a mine it becomes Detonated, struck_cell_id holds its id, status becomes Lost, ended_at is set and elapsed_seconds freezes. When the last non-mine cell is opened, status becomes Won, ended_at is set, every mine cell is set to Flagged, flags_placed equals mine_count and remaining_mines is 0. Opening an Opened, Detonated or Flagged cell, or opening any cell in a Won, Lost or Abandoned game, changes nothing and raises no error.

actions.name: toggle_flag
actions.description: Switches a Hidden cell to Flagged (flags_placed +1) or a Flagged cell back to Hidden (flags_placed −1), and is allowed only while status is Ready or Playing. Afterwards remaining_mines = mine_count − flags_placed, which may go negative; flags are unlimited. Toggling an Opened or Detonated cell, or any cell in a Won, Lost or Abandoned game, changes nothing and raises no error.

actions.name: chord_cell
actions.description: Applies only to an Opened cell with adjacent_mine_count N ≥ 1 while status is Playing. If exactly N of its neighbours are Flagged, every Hidden neighbour is opened exactly as open_cell would, including cascades, a win, or a loss if a neighbour is a mine (that cell becomes Detonated, struck_cell_id is set and status becomes Lost). If the flag count differs from N, the cell is Hidden, Flagged or a zero cell, or the game is not Playing, nothing changes and no error is raised.

actions.name: tick
actions.description: The clock advancing one second: while status is Playing, elapsed_seconds increases by 1, capped at 999. In any other status nothing changes.

actions.name: restart_game
actions.description: Pressing the smiley. If status is Ready or Playing it becomes Abandoned and ended_at is set; if Won or Lost the outcome is kept. Returns a new Game with a new id and the same difficulty_id, width, height and mine_count, in its starting state.

actions.name: change_difficulty
actions.description: Choosing a difficulty from the menu: beginner gives 9×9 with 10 mines, intermediate 16×16 with 40, expert 30×16 with 99. Custom uses the given width (9–30), height (9–24) and mine_count (10 to (width−1)×(height−1)); out-of-range or unknown values raise InvalidConfigurationError and leave this game completely unchanged. When the choice is valid, a Ready or Playing game becomes Abandoned (Won or Lost keep their outcome), and a new Game with a new id and the chosen difficulty_id, width, height and mine_count is returned in its starting state.

actions.name: abandon_game
actions.description: Closing or leaving the game: if status is Ready or Playing it becomes Abandoned, ended_at is set and elapsed_seconds freezes. A Won, Lost or Abandoned game is left unchanged with no error; nothing is ever scored.

actions.name: record_win
actions.description: Applied automatically when a game is Won. For a standard difficulty (beginner, intermediate, expert) where elapsed_seconds < best_seconds, best_seconds becomes elapsed_seconds and game_id and achieved_at are updated; a slower or equal time keeps the stored best. A custom difficulty, or a difficulty_id differing from this record's, changes nothing.

starting_states.description: Constructed with id, difficulty_id, width, height, mine_count, remaining_mines and created_at: status 'Ready', mines_laid False, flags_placed 0, elapsed_seconds 0, remaining_mines equal to mine_count, started_at, ended_at and struck_cell_id None, events empty. cells holds width×height dicts in row-major order, with zero-based row and column and id f"{row}-{column}" (e.g. '0-0'). Each cell has has_mine False, adjacent_mine_count 0 and state 'Hidden'.
Constructed with id, difficulty_id (beginner, intermediate or expert), game_id, best_seconds and achieved_at from the first win of that difficulty; it holds exactly those values, with events empty.

import pytest

from src.domain.game import Game


CREATED_AT = "2024-01-01T10:00:00+00:00"


def _new_game(difficulty_id, width, height, mine_count, game_id="game-1"):
    return Game(
        id=game_id,
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        width=width,
        height=height,
        mine_count=mine_count,
        remaining_mines=mine_count,
        created_at=CREATED_AT,
    )


def _assert_board_shape_and_mines(game, width, height, mine_count, opened_row, opened_column):
    # The board is a width x height rectangle: one cell per (row, column),
    # rows 0..height-1 and columns 0..width-1, nothing more, nothing less.
    assert len(game.cells) == width * height
    positions = {(cell["row"], cell["column"]) for cell in game.cells}
    expected_positions = {(r, c) for r in range(height) for c in range(width)}
    assert positions == expected_positions

    # Once laid, exactly mine_count cells hold a mine (auto-flagging on a
    # possible win changes state only, never has_mine).
    assert game.mines_laid is True
    mines = [cell for cell in game.cells if cell["has_mine"]]
    assert len(mines) == mine_count

    # First click is safe: the opened cell never holds one of those mines.
    opened = [
        cell for cell in game.cells
        if cell["row"] == opened_row and cell["column"] == opened_column
    ]
    assert len(opened) == 1
    assert opened[0]["has_mine"] is False


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "difficulty_id, width, height, mine_count",
    [
        ("beginner", 9, 9, 10),
        ("expert", 30, 16, 99),
        ("custom", 12, 20, 25),
    ],
)
def test_laying_mines_places_exactly_mine_count_on_a_width_by_height_board(
    difficulty_id, width, height, mine_count
):
    # Given a newly created Ready game of width W, height H and mine count M
    game = _new_game(difficulty_id, width, height, mine_count)

    # Before laying: W*H cells, none holds a mine.
    assert len(game.cells) == width * height
    assert sum(1 for cell in game.cells if cell["has_mine"]) == 0

    # When the mines are laid by the first open (a cell inside the grid)
    row, column = height // 2, width // 2
    game.open_cell(row=row, column=column)

    # Then the board still has W*H cells, and exactly M of them hold a mine;
    # M <= (W-1)*(H-1) < W*H - 1 so there is always room off the opened cell.
    _assert_board_shape_and_mines(game, width, height, mine_count, row, column)


def test_mine_count_exactly_at_the_maximum_is_accepted_and_fully_laid():
    # Given a beginner game; a Custom 9x9 board allows at most (9-1)*(9-1) = 64 mines
    game = _new_game("beginner", 9, 9, 10)

    # When the player picks Custom 9x9 with exactly 64 mines (at the limit)
    new_game = game.change_difficulty(
        difficulty_id="custom", width=9, height=9, mine_count=64
    )

    # Then it is accepted: a new Ready game with the chosen configuration
    assert new_game.width == 9
    assert new_game.height == 9
    assert new_game.mine_count == 64
    assert new_game.status == "Ready"

    # When its mines are laid by the first open at the centre (4, 4):
    # 80 other cells exist, so all 64 mines fit off the opened cell.
    new_game.open_cell(row=4, column=4)

    # Then the board has 81 cells and exactly 64 of them hold a mine
    _assert_board_shape_and_mines(new_game, 9, 9, 64, 4, 4)


def test_mine_count_just_beyond_the_maximum_is_refused():
    # Given a beginner game; a Custom 9x9 board allows at most 64 mines
    game = _new_game("beginner", 9, 9, 10)

    # When the player picks Custom 9x9 with 65 mines (one beyond the limit)
    with pytest.raises(Exception) as exc_info:
        game.change_difficulty(
            difficulty_id="custom", width=9, height=9, mine_count=65
        )

    # Then the configuration is refused and the current game is unchanged
    assert type(exc_info.value).__name__ == "InvalidConfigurationError"
    assert game.status == "Ready"
    assert game.difficulty_id == "beginner"
    assert game.width == 9
    assert game.height == 9
    assert game.mine_count == 10
    assert len(game.cells) == 81
    assert sum(1 for cell in game.cells if cell["has_mine"]) == 0

import pytest

from src.domain.game import Game


CREATED_AT = "2024-01-01T10:00:00+00:00"


def _make_ready_game(game_id, difficulty_id, width, height, mine_count):
    game = Game(
        id=game_id,
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        width=width,
        height=height,
        mine_count=mine_count,
        remaining_mines=mine_count,
        created_at=CREATED_AT,
    )
    # Starting state of a newly created game: Ready, no mines laid, all cells Hidden.
    game.status = "Ready"
    game.mines_laid = False
    game.flags_placed = 0
    game.elapsed_seconds = 0
    game.remaining_mines = mine_count
    game.started_at = None
    game.ended_at = None
    game.struck_cell_id = None
    game.events = []
    game.cells = [
        {
            "id": f"{row}-{column}",
            "row": row,
            "column": column,
            "has_mine": False,
            "adjacent_mine_count": 0,
            "state": "Hidden",
        }
        for row in range(height)
        for column in range(width)
    ]
    return game


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "start_difficulty, start_width, start_height, start_mines",
    [
        ("intermediate", 16, 16, 40),
        ("expert", 30, 16, 99),
    ],
)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "given_width, given_height, given_mines",
    [
        # exactly the Beginner values
        (9, 9, 10),
        # one beyond each Beginner value: the preset ignores them and stays 9x9 with 10
        (10, 10, 11),
    ],
)
def test_choosing_beginner_creates_9_by_9_game_with_10_mines(
    start_difficulty,
    start_width,
    start_height,
    start_mines,
    given_width,
    given_height,
    given_mines,
):
    game = _make_ready_game("game-1", start_difficulty, start_width, start_height, start_mines)

    new_game = game.change_difficulty(
        difficulty_id="beginner",
        width=given_width,
        height=given_height,
        mine_count=given_mines,
    )

    # Beginner preset: difficulty_id 'beginner', 9 wide, 9 high, 10 mines, whatever
    # width/height/mine_count were passed (those are used only for Custom).
    assert new_game.difficulty_id == "beginner"
    assert new_game.width == 9
    assert new_game.height == 9
    assert new_game.mine_count == 10

    # The new game is in its starting state: Ready, counter = mine_count = 10,
    # nothing flagged, timer 0, no mines laid.
    assert new_game.status == "Ready"
    assert new_game.remaining_mines == 10
    assert new_game.flags_placed == 0
    assert new_game.elapsed_seconds == 0
    assert new_game.mines_laid is False

    # 9 x 9 = 81 cells in row-major order, all Hidden and mine-free before the first open.
    assert len(new_game.cells) == 81
    assert new_game.cells[0]["id"] == "0-0"
    assert new_game.cells[-1]["id"] == "8-8"
    assert all(cell["state"] == "Hidden" for cell in new_game.cells)
    assert all(cell["has_mine"] is False for cell in new_game.cells)

    # It is a new game with a new id.
    assert new_game.id != "game-1"

    # The previous game was Ready, so a valid difficulty choice abandons it.
    assert game.status == "Abandoned"
    assert game.ended_at is not None


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "start_difficulty, start_width, start_height, start_mines",
    [
        ("intermediate", 16, 16, 40),
        ("expert", 30, 16, 99),
    ],
)
def test_misspelled_beginner_is_refused_and_game_unchanged(
    start_difficulty, start_width, start_height, start_mines
):
    game = _make_ready_game("game-1", start_difficulty, start_width, start_height, start_mines)
    before = game.to_dict()

    # 'beginners' is not one of beginner/intermediate/expert/custom: an unknown
    # difficulty_id is refused with InvalidConfigurationError, same values otherwise.
    with pytest.raises(Exception) as exc_info:
        game.change_difficulty(
            difficulty_id="beginners",
            width=9,
            height=9,
            mine_count=10,
        )
    assert type(exc_info.value).__name__ == "InvalidConfigurationError"

    # A refused choice leaves the current game completely unchanged: still Ready,
    # same size, mines, counter, timer and cells.
    assert game.status == "Ready"
    assert game.difficulty_id == start_difficulty
    assert game.width == start_width
    assert game.height == start_height
    assert game.mine_count == start_mines
    assert game.to_dict() == before
